problem: At the corners of an equilateral triangle, three mice are positioned. At time $t = 0$, each mouse begins crawling directly towards the next mouse: Mouse 1 towards Mouse 2, Mouse 2 towards Mouse 3, and Mouse 3 towards Mouse 1. The speed of each mouse is proportional to the distance to the mouse it is chasing. Describe the trajectories of the mice by setting up and solving a system of differential equations. What happens to the positions of the mice as $t \to +\infty$? Use complex numbers to represent the positions of the mice, and choose an appropriate origin for the coordinate system.
pred: z_j(t) = R\,e^{2\pi i(j-1)/3}\;\exp\!\Big[\!\Big(-\tfrac{3k}{2}+i\,\tfrac{\sqrt{3}\,k}{2}\Big)t\Big],\quad j=1,2,3;\qquad \text{as }t\to+\infty,\;z_1,z_2,z_3\to 0 \text{ (logarithmic spiral into the center).}

answer_text:
# Three Mice Chasing Problem via Complex ODEs

## Setting Up the Coordinate System

I place the **origin at the center of the equilateral triangle**. With side-length-adjacent vertices at distance $R$ from the center, the initial positions are:

$$z_1(0) = R, \qquad z_2(0) = R\,e^{2\pi i/3}, \qquad z_3(0) = R\,e^{4\pi i/3}$$

## Deriving the System of ODEs

Mouse 1 crawls toward Mouse 2 with speed proportional to their separation: $|\dot{z}_1| = k\,|z_2 - z_1|$. The direction of motion is $\dfrac{z_2-z_1}{|z_2-z_1|}$, so the velocity is:

$$\dot{z}_1 = k\,|z_2-z_1|\cdot\frac{z_2-z_1}{|z_2-z_1|} = k(z_2 - z_1)$$

By cyclic symmetry:

$$\boxed{\dot{z}_1 = k(z_2-z_1), \qquad \dot{z}_2 = k(z_3-z_2), \qquad \dot{z}_3 = k(z_1-z_3)}$$

## Exploiting the $C_3$ Symmetry

A rotation by $2\pi/3$ about the origin permutes the mice in the same way the equations are labeled, so the equilateral configuration is preserved for all $t$:

$$z_2(t) = e^{2\pi i/3}\,z_1(t), \qquad z_3(t) = e^{4\pi i/3}\,z_1(t)$$

**Verification:** The centroid $\frac{1}{3}(z_1+z_2+z_3)=0$ for all $t$ (its derivative vanishes identically).

## Reducing to a Single ODE

Substituting $z_2 = e^{2\pi i/3}z_1$ into the first equation:

$$\dot{z}_1 = k\!\left(e^{2\pi i/3}-1\right)z_1 = k\!\left(-\tfrac{3}{2}+i\,\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)z_1$$

This is a linear ODE with solution (initial condition $z_1(0)=R$):

$$z_1(t) = R\exp\!\Big[\!\Big(-\tfrac{3k}{2}+i\,\tfrac{\sqrt{3}\,k}{2}\Big)t\Big] = R\,e^{-3kt/2}\;e^{\,i\sqrt{3}\,kt/2}$$

## The Three Trajectories

$$z_1(t) = R\,e^{-3kt/2}\;e^{\,i\sqrt{3}\,kt/2}$$
$$z_2(t) = R\,e^{2\pi i/3}\;e^{-3kt/2}\;e^{\,i\sqrt{3}\,kt/2}$$
$$z_3(t) = R\,e^{4\pi i/3}\;e^{-3kt/2}\;e^{\,i\sqrt{3}\,kt/2}$$

## Identifying the Spiral Shape

Writing $z_1 = re^{i\theta}$:
$$r(t) = R\,e^{-3kt/2}, \qquad \theta(t) = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}\,k}{2}\,t$$

Eliminating $t$:
$$\theta = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\ln\!\frac{r}{R} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad r = R\,e^{-\theta/\sqrt{3}}$$

This is a **logarithmic (equiangular) spiral**. The angle $\psi$ between the velocity and the inward radial direction satisfies $\tan\psi = \dfrac{r\,\dot\theta}{|\dot r|} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{3/2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $\psi = 30°$—exactly the angle a side makes with the median in an equilateral triangle, as expected geometrically.

## Behavior as $t\to+\infty$

Since $e^{-3kt/2}\to 0$ exponentially:

- The **equilateral triangle shrinks** with side length $\sqrt{3}\,R\,e^{-3kt/2}\to 0$.
- The triangle **rotates** with angular velocity $\omega = \frac{\sqrt{3}\,k}{2}$.
- All three mice **converge to the origin** (the center of the triangle) along logarithmic spiral paths.

$$\lim_{t\to+\infty} z_j(t) = 0, \qquad j=1,2,3$$

The mice spiral inward, the triangle collapses to a point, and the process never "completes" in finite time—the convergence is purely exponential.

$$\boxed{z_j(t) = R\,e^{2\pi i(j-1)/3}\;\exp\!\Big[\!\Big(-\tfrac{3k}{2}+i\,\tfrac{\sqrt{3}\,k}{2}\Big)t\Big],\quad j=1,2,3;\qquad \text{as }t\to+\infty,\;z_1,z_2,z_3\to 0 \text{ (logarithmic spiral into the center).}}$$
